secondary: Sulfur supports protein formation; test before applying.
micronutrients: Check zinc and iron if local tests or symptoms indicate a problem.
wheat.organicMatter: Retain residues where practical; no universal organic matter target.
nutrientNotes: Excess nitrogen can increase lodging risk; rates require yield goals and soil tests.
wheat.residue: Cereal residues can return carbon when retained; nutrient removal rises if straw is exported.

secondary: Check sulfur on low organic matter or sandy soils.
micronutrients: Zinc deficiency can limit maize; use a local lab interpretation.
maize.organicMatter: Residue retention can contribute carbon; no universal target.
nutrientNotes: Nitrogen and potassium supply need testing; silage exports more biomass than grain alone.
maize.residue: Retained stalks can support organic matter; silage harvest removes most above-ground residue.

secondary: Sulfur supply and nitrogen management affect grain quality.
micronutrients: Use local tissue/soil tests to assess micronutrient needs.
barley.organicMatter: Retain straw if compatible with management; no universal target.
nutrientNotes: Nitrogen needs depend on feed versus malting use; excess can harm quality.
barley.residue: Straw retention adds carbon; it does not establish a measured nutrient credit.

secondary: Calcium, magnesium and sulfur need local soil-test interpretation.
micronutrients: Iron chlorosis can occur on calcareous soils; avoid blanket micronutrient treatments.
soybean.organicMatter: Manage residues and cover crops; no universal organic matter target.
nutrientNotes: Effective nodulation can supply nitrogen, but harvested beans remove substantial N. A net soil N gain is not guaranteed.
Fixation does not replace phosphorus or potassium removed at harvest.
soybean.residue: A legume changes the rotation; account for grain export before assuming a nitrogen credit.

secondary: Sulfur risk is greater in low organic matter sandy soils.
micronutrients: Do not apply boron in contact with seed; confirm deficiency before treatment.
sunflower.organicMatter: Assess organic matter together with texture and sulfur tests.
nutrientNotes: Rooting depth does not make water or nutrients unlimited; test P, K and N.
sunflower.residue: Residues can contribute carbon if retained; assess broadleaf disease carryover.

secondary: Calcium, magnesium and sulfur should be assessed using local soil/tissue tests.
micronutrients: Iron, zinc and boron require diagnosis; avoid untested applications.
potato.organicMatter: Organic matter can improve water holding; management must consider tuber disease risk.
nutrientNotes: A relatively shallow root system and high nutrient demand make soil and tissue testing important.
Excess nitrogen can delay maturity; tuber removal exports nutrients.
potato.residue: Disturbance and tuber export make cover crops and erosion protection important.

secondary: Calcium supply and steady water uptake matter for fruit quality.
Check magnesium where the soil test indicates a shortage.
micronutrients: Iron, zinc and boron applications need local diagnosis.
tomato.organicMatter: Compost or green manure can help soil condition; test nutrient content.
nutrientNotes: Use soil tests for P, K, Ca and Mg; too much nitrogen can promote vegetation over fruit.
Uneven water uptake can cause calcium-related fruit disorders even when soil calcium is adequate.
tomato.residue: Use non-solanaceous breaks and manage infected residues.
